overall_structure.value: Dual-phase δ-ferrite + austenite matrix with lenticular martensite formed by water quenching; dendritic structures completely eliminated by further soaking at higher temperature; grains of both phases elongated along the rolling direction. Remaining austenite after water quenching is termed untransformed austenite.

source.reason: HRQ microstructure described from Fig. 3 optical/SEM/EBSD images and the results text: dendritic structure eliminated, δ-ferrite and α/γ elongated along RD, part of austenite transformed to lenticular martensite.

unmapped_findings: Martensite start (Ms) temperature of the HRQ condition calculated according to an empirical equation is ~350 °C, supporting the transformation of austenite to martensite due to water quenching (block b0038).

EDS of the HRQ specimen: Mn and Al concentration in δ-ferrite are 7.02±0.25 wt.% and 5.61±0.11 wt.%; in austenite/martensite they are 8.36±0.16 wt.% and 4.75±0.11 wt.%, showing Mn enrichment in austenite/martensite and Al enrichment in δ-ferrite (block b0038, figure_003).

HRQ austenite volume fraction: ~19% before tensile test and ~18% after tensile test; transformation ratio ~5.5%; mechanical stability parameter K ≈ 3.26 (3.216 in Fig. 7c), indicating very stable austenite due to C and Mn diffusion accelerated by δ-ferrite (blocks b0054, b0061, figure_007).
HRQ product of strength and elongation (PSE) = 1.01 GPa% (Hot Rolled row of Table 3), the lowest among all studied conditions (block b0057, table_003).
HRQ fracture surface exhibits mainly cleavage and/or flat facet type structure representing a brittle mode of failure due to the high fraction of δ-ferrite (block b0072, figure_011).
The stress-strain plastic region showed no serrations (no TWIP effect), consistent with the high SFE of these alloys (block b0073).

Nanoindentation load-displacement curves indicate a maximum penetration depth of ~550 nm for untransformed austenite versus ~384 nm for martensite under the same 30 mN load, confirming martensite is the harder phase (block b0044, table_002).

The HRQ specimen's higher YS (486±6 MPa) and UTS (674±20 MPa) with lowest TE (1.5±0.5 %) are attributed to the presence of hard martensite along with retained austenite and δ-ferrite in the microstructure (block b0046).
